ORBIT Health is an intelligent health-monitoring platform designed to support astronaut health and well-being during space missions. It combines IoT hardware, cloud infrastructure, a web-based monitoring dashboard, rule-based health analysis, and machine learning into one integrated ecosystem.

Readings are securely transmitted to the cloud, where they are stored, visualized, and analyzed. The platform provides historical health tracking, automated alerts, health insights, multi-device management, and administrative monitoring. By combining hardware integration, centralized data management, automated analysis, and anomaly detection, it aims to help identify potential health concerns earlier and support more informed medical decisions during space missions.
details:
ORBIT Health is an integrated health-monitoring ecosystem designed to support astronaut health and well-being during space missions. It combines IoT hardware, cloud computing, a web-based health management platform, rule-based analysis, and machine learning to provide continuous health data monitoring and intelligent insights.

The hardware architecture uses an ESP32 microcontroller to collect physiological data from sensors such as the MAX30001 ECG and heart-rate sensor and TMP temperature sensors. A DS18B20 temperature sensor is also used in the current hardware simulation. The collected readings are securely transmitted to the cloud, where they are stored and processed.

The web platform allows users to monitor vital signs, visualize historical readings, track health trends, receive automated alerts, and access health insights. An administrative interface provides centralized monitoring and management capabilities. The machine learning component uses an Isolation Forest model to identify potentially abnormal patterns in physiological data.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to help address the challenges of monitoring astronaut health in isolated environments where immediate medical assistance may be limited. Automated monitoring, anomaly detection, and centralized health records can support earlier identification of unusual health patterns, improve situational awareness, and assist mission support personnel in making informed decisions.

Technologies and Tools

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
  • Backend: Next.js API routes, Python, FastAPI
  • Database and Cloud: Supabase, PostgreSQL, Vercel, Render
  • Machine Learning: Python, Scikit-learn, Pandas, Isolation Forest
  • Hardware: ESP32, MAX30001, TMP temperature sensors, DS18B20
  • Development and Simulation: Arduino/C++, Wokwi, Git, GitHub

Creativity and Innovation

ORBIT Health brings hardware-based monitoring, cloud-connected health management, rule-based alerts, and machine learning anomaly detection into a single ecosystem. Its modular architecture allows additional sensors and monitoring devices to be integrated as the project evolves. Multi-user and multi-device management also makes it more adaptable than a standalone monitoring device.

Design Considerations

Key considerations include data reliability, secure device authentication, user privacy, sensor compatibility, scalability, response time, and the limitations of automated health predictions. The system is designed to distinguish between rule-based health alerts and machine learning anomaly detection, while treating both as decision-support tools rather than medical diagnoses.
